n: The battle Samuel foretold takes place. Israel's army flees before the Philistines, and many fall dead on Mount Gilboa.
The Philistines close in on Saul and his sons, killing Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua. Faithful Jonathan dies beside his father, loyal to the end.

f.g: Possibly the same as Ishui in 1 Samuel 14:49.

n: The fighting turns hard against Saul, and archers find him, wounding him badly.

f.g: Or “greatly terrified” — the Hebrew can mean either.

n: Saul begs his armor-bearer to kill him so the uncircumcised Philistines won't torture and humiliate him. The armor-bearer refuses out of fear, so Saul falls on his own sword.

f.g: mock, torture, make sport of me

n: When the armor-bearer sees Saul dead, he too falls on his sword and dies with him.
Saul, three of his sons, his armor-bearer, and his men all die that same day, fulfilling the words spoken at En-dor. Israel's first king ends in tragedy.
Israelites living across the valley and beyond the Jordan see the defeat and abandon their towns. The Philistines move in. Israel is at its lowest point — setting the stage for David's rise.
The next day, when the Philistines come to strip the dead, they find Saul and his three sons on Mount Gilboa.

f.g: to take weapons and valuables from the dead

n: They cut off Saul's head and take his armor, sending news of the victory throughout Philistia to their temples and people — a cruel reversal of David's victory over Goliath.

f.g: proclaim it, announce the good news

n: They put Saul's armor in the temple of Ashtoreth and hang his body on the wall of Beth-shan as a public display of humiliation.

f.g: A fortified city at the junction of the Jezreel and Jordan valleys; its ruins are a major archaeological site today.

n: The people of Jabesh-gilead hear what the Philistines have done to Saul's body. They remember that Saul's first act as king was to rescue their city.
Their bravest men march all night, take down the bodies of Saul and his sons from the wall, and bring them to Jabesh, where they burn them — perhaps because the bodies were mutilated.

f.g: A risky journey of over ten miles into enemy-controlled territory.

n: They bury the bones under a tree at Jabesh and fast seven days in mourning. Their loyalty honors the king who once saved them. David later blesses them for it.

f.w: buried them under a tree at Jabesh
